# Context:
Each of five students—Hubert, Lori, Paul, Regina, and Sharon—will visit exactly one of three cities—Montreal, Toronto, or Vancouver—for the month of March, according to the following conditions: Sharon visits a different city than Paul. Hubert visits the same city as Regina. Lori visits Montreal or else Toronto. If Paul visits Vancouver, Hubert visits Vancouver with him. Each student visits one of the cities with at least one of the other four students.

# Question:
Which one of the following could be true for March?

# Options:
A) Hubert, Lori, and Paul visit Toronto, and Regina and Sharon visit Vancouver.
B) Hubert, Lori, Paul, and Regina visit Montreal, and Sharon visits Vancouver.
C) Hubert, Paul, and Regina visit Toronto, and Lori and Sharon visit Montreal.
D) Hubert, Regina, and Sharon visit Montreal, and Lori and Paul visit Vancouver.
E) Lori, Paul, and Sharon visit Montreal, and Hubert and Regina visit Toronto.

from z3 import *

# Declarations
# Each of five students—Hubert, Lori, Paul, Regina, and Sharon—will visit exactly one of three cities—Montreal, Toronto, or Vancouver—for the month of March.
students_sort, (Hubert, Lori, Paul, Regina, Sharon) = EnumSort('students', ['Hubert', 'Lori', 'Paul', 'Regina', 'Sharon'])
cities_sort, (Montreal, Toronto, Vancouver) = EnumSort('cities', ['Montreal', 'Toronto', 'Vancouver'])
students = [Hubert, Lori, Paul, Regina, Sharon]
cities = [Montreal, Toronto, Vancouver]
visit = Function('visit', students_sort, cities_sort)

# Pre_Conditions
pre_conditions = []
# Each of five students—Hubert, Lori, Paul, Regina, and Sharon—will visit exactly one of three cities—Montreal, Toronto, or Vancouver—for the month of March.
s = Const('s', students_sort)
c = Const('c', cities_sort)
pre_conditions.append(ForAll([s], Exists([c], visit(s) == c)))
# Sharon visits a different city than Paul.
pre_conditions.append(visit(Sharon) != visit(Paul))
# Hubert visits the same city as Regina.
pre_conditions.append(visit(Hubert) == visit(Regina))
# Lori visits Montreal or else Toronto.
pre_conditions.append(Or(visit(Lori) == Montreal, visit(Lori) == Toronto))
# If Paul visits Vancouver, Hubert visits Vancouver with him.
pre_conditions.append(Implies(visit(Paul) == Vancouver, visit(Hubert) == Vancouver))
# Each student visits one of the cities with at least one of the other four students.
s = Const('s', students_sort)
o = Const('o', students_sort)
pre_conditions.append(ForAll([s], Exists([o], And(s != o, visit(s) == visit(o)))))

# Question: Which one of the following could be true for March?
def is_sat(option_constraints):
    solver = Solver()
    solver.add(pre_conditions)
    solver.add(option_constraints)
    return solver.check() == sat


# A) Hubert, Lori, and Paul visit Toronto, and Regina and Sharon visit Vancouver.
if is_sat(And(visit(Hubert) == Toronto, visit(Lori) == Toronto, visit(Paul) == Toronto, visit(Regina) == Vancouver, visit(Sharon) == Vancouver)): print('(A)')
# B) Hubert, Lori, Paul, and Regina visit Montreal, and Sharon visits Vancouver.
if is_sat(And(visit(Hubert) == Montreal, visit(Lori) == Montreal, visit(Paul) == Montreal, visit(Regina) == Montreal, visit(Sharon) == Vancouver)): print('(B)')
# C) Hubert, Paul, and Regina visit Toronto, and Lori and Sharon visit Montreal.
if is_sat(And(visit(Hubert) == Toronto, visit(Paul) == Toronto, visit(Regina) == Toronto, visit(Lori) == Montreal, visit(Sharon) == Montreal)): print('(C)')
# D) Hubert, Regina, and Sharon visit Montreal, and Lori and Paul visit Vancouver.
if is_sat(And(visit(Hubert) == Montreal, visit(Regina) == Montreal, visit(Sharon) == Montreal, visit(Lori) == Vancouver, visit(Paul) == Vancouver)): print('(D)')
# E) Lori, Paul, and Sharon visit Montreal, and Hubert and Regina visit Toronto.
if is_sat(And(visit(Lori) == Montreal, visit(Paul) == Montreal, visit(Sharon) == Montreal, visit(Hubert) == Toronto, visit(Regina) == Toronto)): print('(E)')

# Context:
A soft drink manufacturer surveyed consumer preferences for exactly seven proposed names for its new soda: Jazz, Kola, Luck, Mist, Nipi, Oboy, and Ping. The manufacturer ranked the seven names according to the number of votes they received. The name that received the most votes was ranked first. Every name received a different number of votes. Some of the survey results are as follows: Jazz received more votes than Oboy. Oboy received more votes than Kola. Kola received more votes than Mist. Nipi did not receive the fewest votes. Ping received fewer votes than Luck but more votes than Nipi and more votes than Oboy.

# Question:
Which one of the following statements must be true?

# Options:
A) Jazz received more votes than Nipi.
B) Kola received more votes than Nipi.
C) Luck received more votes than Jazz.
D) Nipi received more votes than Oboy.
E) Ping received more votes than Kola.

from z3 import *

# Declarations
# A soft drink manufacturer surveyed consumer preferences for exactly seven proposed names for its new soda: Jazz, Kola, Luck, Mist, Nipi, Oboy, and Ping. The manufacturer ranked the seven names according to the number of votes they received. The name that received the most votes was ranked first. Every name received a different number of votes.
names_sort, (Jazz, Kola, Luck, Mist, Nipi, Oboy, Ping) = EnumSort('names', ['Jazz', 'Kola', 'Luck', 'Mist', 'Nipi', 'Oboy', 'Ping'])
names = [Jazz, Kola, Luck, Mist, Nipi, Oboy, Ping]
votes = Function('votes', names_sort, IntSort())

# Pre_Conditions
pre_conditions = []
# Every name received a different number of votes.
n1 = Const('n1', names_sort)
n2 = Const('n2', names_sort)
pre_conditions.append(ForAll([n1, n2], Implies(n1 != n2, votes(n1) != votes(n2))))
# Jazz received more votes than Oboy.
pre_conditions.append(votes(Jazz) > votes(Oboy))
# Oboy received more votes than Kola.
pre_conditions.append(votes(Oboy) > votes(Kola))
# Kola received more votes than Mist.
pre_conditions.append(votes(Kola) > votes(Mist))
# Nipi did not receive the fewest votes.
n = Const('n', names_sort)
pre_conditions.append(Exists([n], votes(Nipi) > votes(n)))
# Ping received fewer votes than Luck but more votes than Nipi and more votes than Oboy.
pre_conditions.append(And(votes(Ping) < votes(Luck), votes(Ping) > votes(Nipi), votes(Ping) > votes(Oboy)))

# Question: Which one of the following statements must be true?
def is_valid(option_constraints):
    solver = Solver()
    solver.add(pre_conditions)
    solver.add(Not(option_constraints))
    return solver.check() == unsat


# A) Jazz received more votes than Nipi.
if is_valid(votes(Jazz) > votes(Nipi)): print('(A)')
# B) Kola received more votes than Nipi.
if is_valid(votes(Kola) > votes(Nipi)): print('(B)')
# C) Luck received more votes than Jazz.
if is_valid(votes(Luck) > votes(Jazz)): print('(C)')
# D) Nipi received more votes than Oboy.
if is_valid(votes(Nipi) > votes(Oboy)): print('(D)')
# E) Ping received more votes than Kola.
if is_valid(votes(Ping) > votes(Kola)): print('(E)')

A small software firm has four offices, numbered 1, 2, 3, and 4. Each of its offices has exactly one computer and exactly one printer. Each of these eight machines was bought in either 1987, 1988, or 1989. The eight machines were bought in a manner consistent with the following conditions: The computer in each office was bought either in an earlier year than or in the same year as the printer in that office. The computer in office 2 and the printer in office 1 were bought in the same year. The computer in office 3 and the printer in office 4 were bought in the same year. The computer in office 2 and the computer in office 3 were bought in different years. The computer in office 1 and the printer in office 3 were bought in 1988.

# Question:
Which one of the following statements could be true?

# Options:
A) The printer in office 1 was bought in 1987.
B) The computer in office 2 was bought in 1987.
C) The computer in office 3 was bought in 1989.
D) The printer in office 4 was bought in 1988.
E) The printer in office 4 was bought in 1989.
chosen_program:
from z3 import *

# Declarations
# A small software firm has four offices, numbered 1, 2, 3, and 4. Each of its offices has exactly one computer and exactly one printer. Each of these eight machines was bought in either 1987, 1988, or 1989.
offices_sort = IntSort()
years_sort = IntSort()
computers_sort, (c1, c2, c3, c4) = EnumSort('computers', ['c1', 'c2', 'c3', 'c4'])
printers_sort, (p1, p2, p3, p4) = EnumSort('printers', ['p1', 'p2', 'p3', 'p4'])
offices = [1, 2, 3, 4]
years = [1987, 1988, 1989]
computers = [c1, c2, c3, c4]
printers = [p1, p2, p3, p4]
computer_year = Function('computer_year', computers_sort, years_sort)
printer_year = Function('printer_year', printers_sort, years_sort)

# Pre_Conditions
pre_conditions = []
# The computer in each office was bought either in an earlier year than or in the same year as the printer in that office.
pre_conditions.append(And([computer_year(computers[o-1]) <= printer_year(printers[o-1]) for o in offices]))
# The computer in office 2 and the printer in office 1 were bought in the same year.
pre_conditions.append(computer_year(c2) == printer_year(p1))
# The computer in office 3 and the printer in office 4 were bought in the same year.
pre_conditions.append(computer_year(c3) == printer_year(p4))
# The computer in office 2 and the computer in office 3 were bought in different years.
pre_conditions.append(computer_year(c2) != computer_year(c3))
# The computer in office 1 and the printer in office 3 were bought in 1988.
pre_conditions.append(And(computer_year(c1) == 1988, printer_year(p3) == 1988))
c0 = Const('c0', computers_sort)
pre_conditions.append(ForAll([c0], And(1987 <= computer_year(c0), computer_year(c0) <= 1989)))
p0 = Const('p0', printers_sort)
pre_conditions.append(ForAll([p0], And(1987 <= printer_year(p0), printer_year(p0) <= 1989)))

# Question: Which one of the following statements could be true?
def is_sat(option_constraints):
    solver = Solver()
    solver.add(pre_conditions)
    solver.add(option_constraints)
    return solver.check() == sat

# A) The printer in office 1 was bought in 1987.
if is_sat(printer_year(p1) == 1987): print('(A)')
# B) The computer in office 2 was bought in 1987.
if is_sat(computer_year(c2) == 1987): print('(B)')
# C) The computer in office 3 was bought in 1989.
if is_sat(computer_year(c3) == 1989): print('(C)')
# D) The printer in office 4 was bought in 1988.
if is_sat(printer_year(p4) == 1988): print('(D)')
# E) The printer in office 4 was bought in 1989.
if is_sat(printer_year(p4) == 1989): print('(E)')

from z3 import *

# Declarations
# A small software firm has four offices, numbered 1, 2, 3, and 4. Each of its offices has exactly one computer and exactly one printer. Each of these eight machines was bought in either 1987, 1988, or 1989.
offices_sort = IntSort()
years_sort = IntSort()
computers_sort, (c1, c2, c3, c4) = EnumSort('computers', ['c1', 'c2', 'c3', 'c4'])
printers_sort, (p1, p2, p3, p4) = EnumSort('printers', ['p1', 'p2', 'p3', 'p4'])
offices = [1, 2, 3, 4]
years = [1987, 1988, 1989]
computers = [c1, c2, c3, c4]
printers = [p1, p2, p3, p4]
computer_year = Function('computer_year', computers_sort, years_sort)
printer_year = Function('printer_year', printers_sort, years_sort)

# Pre_Conditions
pre_conditions = []
# The computer in each office was bought either in an earlier year than or in the same year as the printer in that office.
pre_conditions.append(And([computer_year(computers[o-1]) <= printer_year(printers[o-1]) for o in offices]))
# The computer in office 2 and the printer in office 1 were bought in the same year.
pre_conditions.append(computer_year(c2) == printer_year(p1))
# The computer in office 3 and the printer in office 4 were bought in the same year.
pre_conditions.append(computer_year(c3) == printer_year(p4))
# The computer in office 2 and the computer in office 3 were bought in different years.
pre_conditions.append(computer_year(c2) != computer_year(c3))
# The computer in office 1 and the printer in office 3 were bought in 1988.
pre_conditions.append(And(computer_year(c1) == 1988, printer_year(p3) == 1988))
c0 = Const('c0', computers_sort)
pre_conditions.append(ForAll([c0], And(1987 <= computer_year(c0), computer_year(c0) <= 1989)))
p0 = Const('p0', printers_sort)
pre_conditions.append(ForAll([p0], And(1987 <= printer_year(p0), printer_year(p0) <= 1989)))

# Question: Which one of the following statements could be true?
def is_sat(option_constraints):
    solver = Solver()
    solver.add(pre_conditions)
    solver.add(option_constraints)
    return solver.check() == sat

# A) The printer in office 1 was bought in 1987.
if is_sat(printer_year(p1) == 1987): print('(A)')
# B) The computer in office 2 was bought in 1987.

# C) The computer in office 3 was bought in 1989.
if is_sat(computer_year(c3) == 1989): print('(C)')
# D) The printer in office 4 was bought in 1988.
if is_sat(printer_year(p4) == 1988): print('(D)')
# E) The printer in office 4 was bought in 1989.
if is_sat(printer_year(p4) == 1989): print('(E)')

lines = [1, 2, 3]

m = Const('m', months_sort)
c = Const('c', colors_sort)

The organisms W, X, Y, and Z respond to the antibiotics ferromycin, ganocyclene, and heptocillin in a manner consistent with the following: Each of the organisms responds to at least one of the antibiotics. No organism responds to all three antibiotics. At least two but not all four of the organisms respond to ferromycin. If W responds to any antibiotic, then X responds to that antibiotic. If an organism responds to ferromycin, then it responds to ganocyclene. Y responds to ferromycin.

# Question:
Each of the following can be true EXCEPT:

# Options:
A) W responds to heptocillin.
B) X responds to ganocyclene.
C) X responds to heptocillin.
D) Y responds to heptocillin.
E) Z responds to ganocyclene.
chosen_program:
from z3 import *

# Declarations
# The organisms W, X, Y, and Z respond to the antibiotics ferromycin, ganocyclene, and heptocillin.
organisms_sort, (W, X, Y, Z) = EnumSort('organisms', ['W', 'X', 'Y', 'Z'])
antibiotics_sort, (ferromycin, ganocyclene, heptocillin) = EnumSort('antibiotics', ['ferromycin', 'ganocyclene', 'heptocillin'])
organisms = [W, X, Y, Z]
antibiotics = [ferromycin, ganocyclene, heptocillin]
responds = Function('responds', organisms_sort, antibiotics_sort, BoolSort())

# Pre_Conditions
pre_conditions = []
# Each of the organisms responds to at least one of the antibiotics
o = Const('o', organisms_sort)
a = Const('a', antibiotics_sort)
pre_conditions.append(ForAll([o], Exists([a], responds(o, a))))
# No organism responds to all three antibiotics
o = Const('o', organisms_sort)
pre_conditions.append(ForAll([o], Not(And(responds(o, ferromycin), responds(o, ganocyclene), responds(o, heptocillin)))))
# At least two but not all four of the organisms respond to ferromycin
pre_conditions.append(Sum([responds(o, ferromycin) for o in organisms]) >= 2)
# Not all four of the organisms respond to ferromycin
pre_conditions.append(Sum([responds(o, ferromycin) for o in organisms]) < 4)
# If W responds to any antibiotic, then X responds to that antibiotic
a = Const('a', antibiotics_sort)
pre_conditions.append(ForAll([a], Implies(responds(W, a), responds(X, a))))
# If an organism responds to ferromycin, then it responds to ganocyclene
o = Const('o', organisms_sort)
pre_conditions.append(ForAll([o], Implies(responds(o, ferromycin), responds(o, ganocyclene))))
# Y responds to ferromycin
pre_conditions.append(responds(Y, ferromycin))

# Question: Each of the following can be true EXCEPT:
def is_unsat(option_constraints):
    solver = Solver()
    solver.add(pre_conditions)
    solver.add(option_constraints)
    return solver.check() == unsat


# A) W responds to heptocillin.
if is_unsat(responds(W, heptocillin)): print('(A)')
# B) X responds to ganocyclene.
if is_unsat(responds(X, ganocyclene)): print('(B)')
# C) X responds to heptocillin.
if is_unsat(responds(X, heptocillin)): print('(C)')
# D) Y responds to heptocillin.
if is_unsat(responds(Y, heptocillin)): print('(D)')
# E) Z responds to ganocyclene.
if is_unsat(responds(Z, ganocyclene)): print('(E)')

Eight camp counselors—Fran, George, Henry, Joan, Kathy, Lewis, Nathan, and Olga—must each be assigned to supervise exactly one of three activities—swimming, tennis, and volleyball. The assignment of counselors must conform to the following conditions: Each activity is supervised by at least two, but not more than three, of the eight counselors. Henry supervises swimming. Neither Kathy nor Olga supervises tennis. Neither Kathy nor Nathan supervises the same activity as Joan. If George supervises swimming, both Nathan and Olga supervise volleyball.

# Question:
Which one of the following is an acceptable assignment of the counselors to the activities?

# Options:
A) Swimming: Fran, George, Henry; Tennis: Joan, Lewis; Volleyball: Kathy, Nathan, Olga
B) Swimming: George, Henry, Olga; Tennis: Fran, Joan, Lewis; Volleyball: Kathy, Nathan
C) Swimming: Henry; Tennis: Fran, George, Joan, Lewis; Volleyball: Kathy, Nathan, Olga
D) Swimming: Henry, Joan, Kathy; Tennis: George, Nathan; Volleyball: Fran, Lewis, Olga
E) Swimming: Henry, Nathan; Tennis: Fran, Kathy, Lewis; Volleyball: George, Joan, Olga

from z3 import *

# Declarations
# Eight camp counselors—Fran, George, Henry, Joan, Kathy, Lewis, Nathan, and Olga—must each be assigned to supervise exactly one of three activities—swimming, tennis, and volleyball.
counselors_sort, (Fran, George, Henry, Joan, Kathy, Lewis, Nathan, Olga) = EnumSort('counselors', ['Fran', 'George', 'Henry', 'Joan', 'Kathy', 'Lewis', 'Nathan', 'Olga'])
activities_sort, (swimming, tennis, volleyball) = EnumSort('activities', ['swimming', 'tennis', 'volleyball'])
counselors = [Fran, George, Henry, Joan, Kathy, Lewis, Nathan, Olga]
activities = [swimming, tennis, volleyball]
assigned = Function('assigned', counselors_sort, activities_sort)

# Pre_Conditions
pre_conditions = []
# Each activity is supervised by at least two, but not more than three, of the eight counselors
a = Const('a', activities_sort)
pre_conditions.append(ForAll([a], And(Sum([assigned(c) == a for c in counselors]) >= 2, Sum([assigned(c) == a for c in counselors]) <= 3)))
# Henry supervises swimming
pre_conditions.append(assigned(Henry) == swimming)
# Neither Kathy nor Olga supervises tennis
pre_conditions.append(And(assigned(Kathy) != tennis, assigned(Olga) != tennis))
# Neither Kathy nor Nathan supervises the same activity as Joan
pre_conditions.append(And(assigned(Kathy) != assigned(Joan), assigned(Nathan) != assigned(Joan)))
# If George supervises swimming, both Nathan and Olga supervise volleyball
pre_conditions.append(Implies(assigned(George) == swimming, And(assigned(Nathan) == volleyball, assigned(Olga) == volleyball)))

# Question: Which one of the following is an acceptable assignment of the counselors to the activities?
def is_sat(option_constraints):
    solver = Solver()
    solver.add(pre_conditions)
    solver.add(option_constraints)
    return solver.check() == sat


# A) Swimming: Fran, George, Henry; Tennis: Joan, Lewis; Volleyball: Kathy, Nathan, Olga
if is_sat(And(assigned(Fran) == swimming, assigned(George) == swimming, assigned(Henry) == swimming, assigned(Joan) == tennis, assigned(Lewis) == tennis, assigned(Kathy) == volleyball, assigned(Nathan) == volleyball, assigned(Olga) == volleyball)): print('(A)')

# D) Swimming: Henry, Joan, Kathy; Tennis: George, Nathan; Volleyball: Fran, Lewis, Olga
if is_sat(And(assigned(Henry) == swimming, assigned(Joan) == swimming, assigned(Kathy) == swimming, assigned(George) == tennis, assigned(Nathan) == tennis, assigned(Fran) == volleyball, assigned(Lewis) == volleyball, assigned(Olga) == volleyball)): print('(D)')
# E) Swimming: Henry, Nathan; Tennis: Fran, Kathy, Lewis; Volleyball: George, Joan, Olga

# Context:
From a group of seven people—J, K, L, M, N, P, and Q—exactly four will be selected to attend a diplomat's retirement dinner. Selection must conform to the following conditions: Either J or K must be selected, but J and K cannot both be selected. Either N or P must be selected, but N and P cannot both be selected. N cannot be selected unless L is selected. Q cannot be selected unless K is selected.

# Question:
Which one of the following could be the four people selected to attend the retirement dinner?

# Options:
A) J, K, M, P
B) J, L, N, Q
C) J, M, N, Q
D) K, M, P, Q
E) L, M, N, P

from z3 import *

# Declarations
# From a group of seven people—J, K, L, M, N, P, and Q—exactly four will be selected to attend a diplomat's retirement dinner.
people_sort, (J, K, L, M, N, P, Q) = EnumSort('people', ['J', 'K', 'L', 'M', 'N', 'P', 'Q'])
people = [J, K, L, M, N, P, Q]
selected = Function('selected', people_sort, BoolSort())

# Pre_Conditions
pre_conditions = []
# exactly four people will be selected
pre_conditions.append(Sum([selected(p) for p in people]) == 4)
# Either J or K must be selected
pre_conditions.append(Or(selected(J), selected(K)))
# J and K cannot both be selected
pre_conditions.append(Not(And(selected(J), selected(K))))
# Either N or P must be selected
pre_conditions.append(Or(selected(N), selected(P)))
# N and P cannot both be selected
pre_conditions.append(Not(And(selected(N), selected(P))))
# N cannot be selected unless L is selected
pre_conditions.append(Implies(selected(N), selected(L)))
# Q cannot be selected unless K is selected
pre_conditions.append(Implies(selected(Q), selected(K)))

# Question: Which one of the following could be the four people selected to attend the retirement dinner?
def is_sat(option_constraints):
    solver = Solver()
    solver.add(pre_conditions)
    solver.add(option_constraints)
    return solver.check() == sat


# A) J, K, M, P
if is_sat(And(selected(J), selected(K), selected(M), selected(P))): print('(A)')
# B) J, L, N, Q
if is_sat(And(selected(J), selected(L), selected(N), selected(Q))): print('(B)')
# C) J, M, N, Q
if is_sat(And(selected(J), selected(M), selected(N), selected(Q))): print('(C)')
# D) K, M, P, Q
if is_sat(And(selected(K), selected(M), selected(P), selected(Q))): print('(D)')
# E) L, M, N, P
if is_sat(And(selected(L), selected(M), selected(N), selected(P))): print('(E)')
